des.title: Design Education Series
des.first: A very large black DES mark dominates a pale field. Navigation and course metadata sit at a much smaller scale; the contrast makes the identity unmistakable, but the immediate learning action is less prominent.
profile: Composition
A strong vertical division, oversized letterforms, thin horizontal rules and large empty intervals establish a deliberate grid.
Typography
The identity is an active compositional object. Small metadata stays systematic while titles become the major landmarks.
Colour and material
Near-monochrome architecture unifies stone, fabric and sculptural course artwork. Colour is reserved for individual objects rather than repeated interface chrome.
Rhythm and density
The page alternates broad quiet space with large course imagery. This is a browsing rhythm, not the density of a daily practice workspace.
Motion
The recorded entrance and scroll reveal change the spatial composition. Course imagery is staged as a sequence; exact easing and performance are not established.
Identity
The same geometry, material treatment and type relationships recur across the inspected homepage. Creator intent connects the identity to organizing fragmented knowledge.
des.strengths: Distinctive typography, consistent art direction and related course imagery make the page recognizable without a large collection of decorative components.
des.limits: The generic mobile wheel sequence did not move the page; its initial mobile frames only establish the entry composition. The touch-specific follow-up reached the introduction and course card; see the interaction register. Desktop Home/scrollTo did not reliably return the custom-scrolling page to its initial state. Neither observation is proof that ordinary user scrolling is broken. Small metadata and expansive gaps require a different treatment in time-sensitive GTOP tasks.
des.transfer: Use the principle of a recognizable typographic hierarchy and subject-specific visual language for the public entry and lab introductions. Preserve compact, direct controls inside practice. Do not adopt the identity, assets, long staging or extreme empty space.
des.controls: Desktop slow/fast/reverse scroll observed in the recording; mobile touch follow-up in the interaction register. Private courses and checkout were not entered.
des.source: Creator context: [Obys case study](https://tympanus.net/codrops/2024/08/21/case-study-design-education-series/). The designers describe fragmented knowledge becoming an organized identity. That is stated intent, not measured learner response. Award provenance is in the shortlist.

twks.title: twks
twks.first: The live hero gives imagery the entire field and lays a quiet navigation line across it. Below it, emphatic text and an asymmetric case grid carry the identity with very little interface ornament.
profile: Composition
A large indented introduction contrasts with narrow descriptive columns; case imagery alternates size and placement.
Typography
A small range of sans-serif treatments creates hierarchy through scale, line breaks and placement, with fine metadata kept secondary.
Colour and material
The shell stays black and white while each project supplies its own colour and photographic or graphic language.
Rhythm and density
Large intervals give projects individual presence. The projects listing has a stable three-column desktop grid.
Motion
Hero media changes over time in live inspection. The project filter visibly replaces the displayed set and exposes an active filter with Reset.
Identity
Consistent editorial rules contain very diverse project images; coherence comes from the frame around the work.
twks.strengths: Strong content hierarchy and a restrained shell let distinctive subject imagery do the expressive work. Filter state is visible and reversible.
twks.limits: The CI normal-motion hero was often black and some case media did not load. Those regions are not aesthetic benchmarks; the loaded live hero and inspected project grid provide separate evidence. Small grey controls and large gaps are not a complete model for dense admin use. No exact contrast or performance audit was conducted.
twks.transfer: Consider a quiet shared shell around expressive lab/topic imagery. In question banks and reports, make selected filters explicit and provide an obvious reset. Do not carry the sparse agency pacing into everyday admin lists.
twks.controls: Opened Projects, then Services, then Digital. The resulting list showed a Digital chip, an active-filter count and Reset. The selected before/after captures are in the gallery.
twks.source: Primary source is the live site and its public Projects interface. Awwwards attribution is separately bounded in the discovery shortlist.

linear.title: Linear
linear.first: A concise white headline sits above a layered product illustration on an almost-black field. Most interface detail is subdued, allowing a small number of titles and status colours to carry emphasis.
profile: Composition
Hero message precedes a large product frame; later sections repeat a heading, explanation and product illustration relationship.
Typography
Strong headlines and compact neutral supporting text create controlled tiers rather than many competing type styles.
Colour and material
Near-black surface steps, fine outlines, muted labels and isolated status accents create depth with little saturation.
Rhythm and density
The public page alternates explanatory space with dense product imagery. The product illustration is not evidence of a tested application workflow.
Motion
The Product menu expands into categorized navigation; Escape closes it. Recorded page sections appear through normal scrolling.
Identity
Typography, tonal surfaces, corner treatment and restrained product compositions maintain a consistent technical character.
linear.strengths: Layered hierarchy, selective emphasis and stable component treatment make complex material feel organized. The menu groups related destinations with descriptions.
linear.limits: Only the public site was inspected. Private app filtering, editing, empty states and recovery were not tested. On mobile the illustrated desktop product interface is cropped and very small; it must not be treated as an acceptable mobile admin layout. Muted details need contrast measurement before being adopted.
linear.transfer: Apply deliberate surface hierarchy and consistent semantic status accents to GTOP dashboards and admin work. Compare actual GTOP task density with a live component reference such as Primer, not with Linear marketing imagery alone. The dark palette itself is not a requirement.
linear.controls: Opened Product, inspected the grouped overlay, then closed it with Escape. This verifies a bounded navigation behavior, not the underlying product.
linear.source: Primary source is the current public Linear homepage. Its present teams-and-agents positioning is observed content, not an assumed description of earlier versions.

bicycle.title: Bicycle — Bartosz Ciechanowski
bicycle.first: A readable article column leads into a large, simplified bicycle simulation. Colour in prose matches the diagram and its controls, so the visual treatment also carries meaning.
profile: Composition
Explanatory paragraphs sit close to the simulation they explain. Later examples isolate a box and a force before returning to more complex mechanics.
Typography
A steady reading measure and modest heading scale keep prose and diagrams in the same teaching rhythm.
Colour and material
A yellow rider/slider and coloured force terms create visual associations. Neutral ground and simplified objects reduce background competition.
Rhythm and density
Explanation alternates with experimentation. One mechanism is introduced at a time.
Motion
The rider changes pose over time; a slider and camera-drag instruction are visible. Direct slider manipulation is recorded in the supplemental pass.
Identity
The article format stays quiet; recognizable explanatory drawings and consistent semantic colour form its character.
bicycle.strengths: The key reference is correspondence: explanation, control, object and outcome belong to the same concept. Mobile retains a readable column and a wide control beneath the illustration.
bicycle.limits: The cloud browser could not initialize this WebGL scene; isolated Chromium rendered it successfully. This is an environment limitation, not proof of a site defect. Software-rendered recordings are not performance measurements. This 2023 article is a teaching-mechanism reference, not a current-fashion claim. No learning benefit was measured.
bicycle.transfer: For plant and electrical/current labs, align the control with the visible mechanism and explain the resulting change nearby. Preserve causal meaning when motion is reduced. Avoid making 3D a requirement when a clearer 2D representation suffices.
bicycle.controls: Final slider capture run 37895866895 verifies visible right/left knob movement and rider-orientation changes in desktop and emulated mobile. The first manipulation attempt did not change the knob and remains diagnostic.
bicycle.source: Primary source is the article and its visible publication date, 28 March 2023. Do not infer student outcomes from the author’s explanatory presentation.

trust.title: The Evolution of Trust
trust.first: Hand-drawn characters and lettering establish a coherent playful world. In the actual game, a short prompt, two choices and the consequence diagram share a stable central stage.
profile: Composition
The opening has a single Play action. The inspected lesson concentrates the diagram between an explanation and two large answer choices.
Typography
Handwritten text matches the illustrations. Emphasis appears through weight and placement rather than many competing card styles.
Colour and material
Mostly black-and-white drawing makes red/blue player markers and yellow outcome highlights stand out.
Rhythm and density
The learner acts before the next explanation appears. The same scene is reused as the explanation becomes more specific.
Motion
A choice changes the explanatory text and highlights numerical outcomes in the diagram. This is evidence of a state transition with meaning, not merely decorative movement.
Identity
Characters, buttons, cursor emphasis, type and drawing strokes share the same visual language.
trust.strengths: The feedback explains why a choice has a consequence and updates the illustration in place. The learner does not have to mentally connect a distant notification with the changed state.
trust.limits: The inspected portion covers entry and the first choice, not the full approximately 30-minute game. The mobile entry scales the stage down substantially, leaving small footer controls; this is a poor responsive pattern to copy. Handwriting is a stylistic reference, not a readability prescription for long GTOP questions.
trust.transfer: For practice feedback, connect the selected response, correct reasoning and outcome in one stable area. For labs, let a prediction or manipulation reveal its consequence. Keep explicit text labels and accessible controls; the hand-drawn skin is optional.
trust.controls: Play → introductory explanation → play-a-game action → Cooperate. The resulting explanation stated the -1/+3 consequence and highlighted it alongside the 0/0 alternative. Before/after screenshots were visually verified.
trust.source: Primary source is the live game, which credits Nicky Case and July 2017. It is retained for teaching interaction, not recency or an award claim.

primer.title: GitHub Primer DataTable
primer.first: A quiet table uses alignment, row spacing and restrained rules to make many values comparable. The sort control changes both its arrow and the row order.
profile: Composition
The documentation shell separates navigation, examples and in-page contents. Within the table, repeated column alignment does most of the organizing work.
Typography
Row names carry more emphasis than supplementary values. Labels remain compact without competing with the page title.
Colour and material
White and light neutral surfaces, thin borders and restrained links provide separation without a colourful card around every value.
Rhythm and density
Consistent rows support scanning. The public documentation shows several density and alignment examples; that is not proof of a whole application’s consistency.
Motion
Repository sorting causes local order and arrow changes; feedback is proportional to the action.
Identity
Precision and consistency supply character. Decorative illustration is unnecessary for this job.
primer.strengths: Sorting has visible, localized feedback. Consistent alignment and row structure make comparison easier to inspect than freely arranged cards.
primer.limits: This is a component demo, not a tested end-to-end admin system. Mobile tables overflow horizontally; the documentation does not establish a complete GTOP small-screen workflow. No broad accessibility or keyboard-conformance claim is made from this limited inspection.
primer.transfer: Use this as an anchor for question-bank, paper, user and log tables: clear column priority, predictable spacing, explicit sorting and status. Decide which columns/actions remain essential on mobile during the GTOP evaluation; do not simply shrink desktop rows.
primer.controls: In the sort example, clicked Repository for ascending order, then again for descending order. The settled screenshots show both the arrow and corresponding row sequence changing.
primer.source: Primary source is the live Primer DataTable documentation and its public examples. No Awwwards status is asserted.

brilliant.title: Brilliant
brilliant.first: A warm background, emphatic serif headline, green action and friendly illustrated teaching demo make the educational proposition feel approachable. The mobile layout changes the order and emphasis of hero material.
profile: Composition
Desktop pairs the learning proposition with a demonstration; mobile places the visual prominently above supporting content.
Typography
Serif display text adds character while sans-serif controls and explanations remain direct.
Colour and material
Warm neutrals, green emphasis, pastel teaching panels and soft corners create a controlled friendly vocabulary.
Rhythm and density
Alternating explanation and demonstration sections keep the public page easy to browse; this is not evidence about paid lesson pacing.
Motion

The hero contains an animated demonstration with a Pause label exposed in the DOM; activation remained unverified. A cursor inside that demonstration is part of the media, not evidence of the reviewer manipulating the lesson.
Identity
Avatar, illustrations, surface colours and typography repeat a coherent educational tone.
brilliant.strengths: Coherent warm typography, illustration and composition make the educational proposition understandable. Playback control is not a verified strength.
brilliant.limits: The initial mobile cookie banner obscured part of the page, so clean-entry and pause/resume states were requested in a supplemental pass. Only public content was inspected; no account, paid lesson, learning effectiveness or student preference is inferred. The current homepage emphasizes Koji; older screenshots should not be substituted for this observed version. Playback control was exposed in the DOM but could not be activated in the attempted path; it is excluded as a positive interaction benchmark.
brilliant.transfer: For public entry and learner introductions, pair a direct promise with relevant educational imagery and a clear primary action. For demonstrations, expose pause/resume and keep the essential explanation available independently of playback.
brilliant.controls: Banner dismissal and clean homepage verified. Pause activation and hover attempts timed out; no pause/resume or subject-tab result is claimed.
brilliant.source: Primary source is the current Brilliant homepage. Marketing statements and app-review totals are not evidence about GTOP learners.
